correctness.rationale: The marked graph is the connected Levi graph of the order-four Latin square: each crosspoint is incident to one line of each class and each distinct-class pair of lines has exactly one common point. Normalizing row and column zero and enumerating gives four reduced squares, exactly the Klein-four table and three simultaneous relabelings of the cyclic table. Their intercalate counts distinguish the two types. Independently I used an oriented incidence matrix with a line vertex removed (rather than rooting at a point as in the deposit), formed the 27×27 integer Gram/Laplacian and performed Smith reduction directly over Z with SymPy. All four gave eighteen 1s and 2,8,8,24,24,24,24,96,96. Replay: `python3 /workspace/net_snf_reproduction.py` with SymPy. The uploaded script and log were read, not run. As an independent check on order, the 12×16 point-incidence block has row Gram matrix with diagonal blocks 4I₄ and off-diagonal all-ones blocks, hence eigenvalues 12, 4 with multiplicity 9, and 0 with multiplicity 2. The block Laplacian matrix-tree product is 7·8⁹·4²·3⁶ divided by 28. The abstract nodal curve is stable since all rational components have valence at least three; its arithmetic genus is 48−28+1. Choosing all smoothing parameters of the form t in an unobstructed deformation gives unit thickness; Raynaud’s degree-class identification applies to this split regular model.
residual_risks: This is not the dual graph of the original union of lines or the full point-line singularity graph. The geometric component group identification does not extend as stated to nonunit thickness or nonsplit special fibers.
